candidates.title: Video2Sim2Real: Full-Stack Autonomous Dexterous Skill Acquisition from a Single Human Video
candidates.abstract: Human manipulation videos are a convenient and intuitive source for robot learning. However, directly transferring human dexterity to robots remains challenging due to perception errors and embodiment gap. To address this, we introduce Video2Sim2Real, a full-stack framework for autonomous skill acquisition from a single human manipulation video. Our framework first uses off-the-shelf foundation models to reconstruct a simulator-ready digital twin and extract robot and object motion priors. Rathe

embodied_relevance.evidence: Full-stack autonomous dexterous skill acquisition from human video to real robot execution across 7 everyday manipulation tasks (apple/peach prep, steak seasoning, toy rearrangement, tissue box, book passing, tray retrieval). Directly advances robot dexterity capability.

primary_source.evidence: Original research paper with novel keyframe refinement strategy, decoupled IL+RL sim-to-real policy, and extensive simulation (91.4% avg success) and real-world evaluation (95.7% success). Not a survey or position paper.

incremental_contribution.evidence: Proposes object-centric keyframe refinement that anchors retargeted motion using optimized robot configurations at sparse keyframes, plus a decoupled policy (IL for geometry gap, residual RL for physics gap). Clear advance over prior RL-only (Residual RL), motion-mimic (Deep-mimic RL), and object-only approaches, which achieve 6-53% vs 91.4%.

claim_support.evidence: Extensive simulation comparisons against 5 RL baselines with 3 seeds each, multi-stage success/safety/jerk metrics. Real-world evaluation against Pure-IL, Pure-RL (finger), Pure-RL (arm+finger) baselines over 5-10 trials per task. Ablation shows distillation-only (33.3%) and residual-only (60%) underperform combined (90%).

fulltext_for_recommendation.evidence: Read full Method (Section 4: Framework with off-the-shelf estimation, keyframe refinement, decoupled sim-to-real, spatial generalization), Experiments (Section 5: refinement evaluation, real-world results, ablation), and Conclusion (Section 6).

candidates.selection_reason: High-quality full pipeline from single human video to robust real-world dexterous manipulation. Keyframe refinement strategy outperforms 5 prior RL-based approaches by large margins (91.4% vs 6-53%). Decoupled IL+RL sim-to-real policy achieves 95.7% real-world success. Strong ablation validates each component. Fills critical gap in autonomous skill acquisition from minimal human supervision. Only weakness: no code release mentioned, limiting reproducibility score.
risks_or_uncertainties: No public code repository or model weights mentioned; reproducibility depends entirely on paper description
Framework relies on multiple off-the-shelf models (Gemini, SAM3, SAM3D, HaMeR, CoTracker) — pipeline fragility if any component degrades
Object meshes assumed available via SAM3D reconstruction; real-world mesh quality varies significantly
Pieter Abbeel NOT an author contrary to task metadata — paper is from Tsinghua/UCSD authors

candidates.title: Mana: Dexterous Manipulation of Articulated Tools
candidates.abstract: Articulated tool manipulation remains a major challenge in dexterous robotics due to the need to coordinate internal degrees of freedom and contact-rich interactions. While prior work has largely focused on rigid objects, articulated tool use remains underexplored because of its physical complexity and the difficulty of learning functional grasping and manipulation policies. We present Mana (Manipulation Animator), a general sim-to-real framework that reinterprets dexterous manipulation as an an

embodied_relevance.evidence: Enables dexterous manipulation of articulated tools (tongs, pliers, clothespins, syringes) with a multi-fingered Allegro hand. Directly addresses the unsolved challenge of coordinated position-force control for functional tool use.

primary_source.evidence: Original research introducing Mana (Manipulation Animator), an animation-inspired sim-to-real data generation framework for articulated tool manipulation. Novel grasp generator + RL-based trajectory generator + point-cloud diffusion policy. Full experimental validation on real hardware.

incremental_contribution.evidence: First framework to handle full pipeline from tabletop grasping to functional in-hand actuation of thin (1cm) articulated tools requiring 3-7N force. Coarse-to-fine approach (keyframes + motion planning + RL) is novel vs prior work limited to rigid objects or requiring fixed initial grasps. Custom fingertip design enables thin-object grasping.

claim_support.evidence: ~70% success rate across 4 tool categories vs teleoperation (~30% on tongs) and open-loop baselines. Ablation shows performance scales with trajectory count and grasp keyframe diversity. Detailed sim-to-real transfer with force calibration and system identification.

fulltext_for_recommendation.evidence: Read Method (Section 3: Mana Data System with grasp generator and trajectory generator), Robot System (Section 4: platform design and visuomotor policy), Experiments (Section 5: main results with Table 1, ablation studies), and Appendix sections for RL details.

candidates.selection_reason: Tackles the long-standing challenge of dexterous articulated tool manipulation with a principled animation-inspired pipeline. Unique insight: reinterpreting manipulation as an animation inbetweening problem enables scalable data generation with minimal human input (<1 minute per tool). Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer across 4 challenging tool types. Co-authored by Pieter Abbeel. Good ablation on data diversity scaling. Slightly weaker on baseline breadth and code availability.
risks_or_uncertainties: Only 2 baselines compared (open-loop Mana, teleoperation via GeoRT); missing comparisons to recent RL-based tool manipulation methods
Success rates ~70% leave substantial room for improvement on real hardware
Tool-to-site transitions still require wrist teleoperation (not fully autonomous)
Custom fingertip design may not transfer to other hands or tools without re-engineering
No explicit code release mentioned

candidates.title: Embodied-R1.5: Evolving Physical Intelligence via Embodied Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: We introduce Embodied-R1.5, a unified Embodied Foundation Model (EFM) that integrates comprehensive embodied reasoning capabilities, spanning embodied cognition, task planning, correction, and pointing, within a single architecture toward general physical intelligence. Leveraging three automated data construction pipelines to significantly expand the data coverage of critical capabilities, we build a large-scale data system of over 15B tokens, and design a multi-task balanced RL recipe to allevi

embodied_relevance.evidence: Unified Embodied Foundation Model (EFM) integrating cognition, task planning, correction, and pointing within a single 8B architecture. Fine-tuned into VLA that outperforms pi_0.5 across 4 manipulation benchmark suites. Zero-shot real-robot experiments cover instruction following, affordance grounding, articulated object manipulation, and long-horizon tasks.

primary_source.evidence: Original research from Tianjin University and Tencent Hunyuan. Introduces three automated data pipelines (15B tokens), multi-task balanced RL recipe, PGC closed-loop framework, and EmbodiedEvalKit. Comprehensive benchmarking across 24 embodied VLM benchmarks + 4 manipulation suites.

incremental_contribution.evidence: Advances from Embodied-R1 (pointing specialist) to a comprehensive EFM unifying 3 capability dimensions. The PGC (Planner-Grounder-Corrector) closed-loop framework enables single-model long-horizon autonomy. Key finding: internalizing embodied reasoning can substitute for large-scale action pretraining — VLA fine-tuned with small action data outperforms pi_0.5 by >20%.

claim_support.evidence: SOTA on 16/24 embodied VLM benchmarks (70.4% avg, surpassing Gemini-Robotics-ER-1.5 by 17% and GPT-5.4 by 21.7%). VLA achieves 92.4% on SimplerEnv. Zero-shot real-robot experiments validate diverse capabilities. Extensive ablation analysis in Section 7.5.

fulltext_for_recommendation.evidence: Read Method (Sections 2-5: architecture, data construction, training strategy, PGC framework), Experiments (Section 7: 5 sub-parts covering VLM benchmarks, manipulation, zero-shot transfer, long-horizon demos, analysis), and Conclusion (Section 9).

candidates.selection_reason: Highest-scoring paper in this batch. Comprehensive EFM with full open-source release (weights, data, code, EmbodiedEvalKit). SOTA on 16/24 benchmarks with only 8B parameters. The PGC closed-loop framework demonstrates genuine long-horizon autonomy. The finding that internalized reasoning reduces action data needs is a significant insight for the field. Fully reproducible infrastructure makes this an exceptional contribution. Note: Danfei Xu is NOT an author (contrary to task metadata) — paper is from Tianjin University / Tencent Hunyuan.
risks_or_uncertainties: Danfei Xu not an author — paper from Tianjin University/Tencent, not Georgia Tech
8B model size may limit capability ceiling on complex physical reasoning
PGC framework validated only on tabletop manipulation; mobile manipulation/navigation not tested
15B token corpus relies heavily on automated pipelines; data quality vs. human annotation tradeoff unclear
VLA fine-tuning requires separate action expert; tighter reasoning-action coupling unexplored

candidates.title: T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
candidates.abstract: The ability to react dynamically to tactile signals has long been considered crucial to agile human-level dexterity. Yet contemporary learning-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic manipulation generally either overlook the tactile modality or are limited to encoders with static cues, due in part to the scarcity of diverse training data and standardized evaluation, architectural constraints in current VLA models, and limitations of static tactile encoders. In this paper, we push

embodied_relevance.evidence: Enables foundational manipulation policies to achieve tactile-reactive dexterous control for contact-rich bimanual tasks. Evaluated on 12 real-world tasks requiring precise force control (egg transfer, lock opening, card extraction, toothpaste application, etc.). Directly advances embodied manipulation capability.

primary_source.evidence: Original research presenting T-Rex model with novel Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts architecture, asynchronous tactile-reactive cascaded flow matching, spatial-temporal VQ-VAE tactile encoding, and 100-hour T-Rex dataset. Full experimental validation across 12 tasks with 6 baselines.

incremental_contribution.evidence: Novel asynchronous tactile-reactive mechanism: slow action expert denoises actions partially, fast tactile expert completes denoising using cached visual context + real-time tactile. VQ-VAE dynamic force encoder compresses temporal force into discrete tokens. Three-stage training recipe (human video pre-training -> tactile mid-training -> task post-training) is novel. 30% improvement over best baseline (EgoScale).

claim_support.evidence: 65% avg success vs 35% (EgoScale, best baseline) across 12 tasks, 16 trials each. Extensive ablations: tactile modality (-23%), async architecture (-5%), mid-training data design, training recipe stages (18%->34%->45%->65%), data efficiency curves. Failure case analysis in Appendix H.

fulltext_for_recommendation.evidence: Read Method (Section 4: T-Rex architecture with MoT, spatial-temporal tactile encoding, asynchronous cascaded flow matching, 3-stage training recipe), Experiments (Section 5: 12-task main results, ablation studies on tactile encoding, async design, data efficiency, training recipe), and Conclusion (Section 6).

candidates.selection_reason: Compelling demonstration that tactile-reactive behaviors can be efficiently acquired through dedicated mid-training rather than requiring tactile data during pre-training. The asynchronous cascaded flow matching elegantly resolves the frequency mismatch between vision (low-rate) and tactile (high-rate) control. 100-hour open-source tactile dataset fills a critical resource gap. Co-authored by Pieter Abbeel. 30% improvement margin over best baseline is substantial. Moderate reproducibility score because dataset is open but model weights not explicitly promised.
risks_or_uncertainties: Model weights not explicitly promised as open-source (dataset is)
Requires specific tactile hardware (Sharpa Wave hands with per-finger force + deformation sensors) — limits adoption
Tactile sensor drift and calibration remain hardware bottlenecks acknowledged by authors
Long-horizon tasks with tight tolerances still challenging for the teleoperation-based approach
12 evaluation tasks may not fully represent diverse tactile-reactive scenarios

candidates.title: SARM2: Multi-Task Stage Aware Reward Modeling for Self Improving Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Fine-tuning vision-language-action (VLA) policies for long-horizon manipulation still relies heavily on behavior cloning, which requires costly high-quality demonstrations and keeps policies near the demonstration distribution. Reward models can reduce this dependence by reweighting demonstrations and providing dense supervision for on-robot reinforcement learning (RL), but they must be dense, accurate, and general. Existing methods fall short: task-specific stage-aware models are accurate but r

embodied_relevance.evidence: Multi-task stage-aware reward model (SARM2) and SPIRAL self-improvement framework for VLA-based robotic manipulation. Evaluated on long-horizon tasks: folding shorts and cleaning whiteboard. Directly advances VLA fine-tuning capability.

primary_source.evidence: Original research introducing SARM2 (action-primitive stage estimator + MMoE value decoder) and SPIRAL (Self-Policy Improvement via Reward-Aligned Learning). Full experimental validation with reward model evaluation on 10 tasks and policy improvement on 2 tasks.

incremental_contribution.evidence: Advances over SARM by making the stage estimator task-agnostic (action-primitive vocabulary shared across tasks) and adding MMoE decoder for multi-task value estimation. SPIRAL framework enables autonomous RL self-improvement without human-in-the-loop corrections. MoE-Decoder placement (in output head vs FFN) is a novel architectural insight.

claim_support.evidence: SARM2 achieves lowest demo MSE (0.020 vs 0.026-0.033 for baselines) across 10 tasks. SPIRAL improves folding shorts from crumpled (4/12 vs 0/12 BC baseline) and cleaning whiteboard (10/20 vs 4/20 BC baseline). Extensive MoE architecture ablations (MoE-Decoder vs MoE-FFN, expert counts, top-k).

fulltext_for_recommendation.evidence: Read Method (Section 3: SARM2 with action-primitive stage estimator and MMoE value decoder, SPIRAL framework), Experimental Results (Section 4: reward model evaluation, policy learning results, analysis), and extensive appendices with MoE design analysis.

candidates.selection_reason: Solid contribution to the VLA self-improvement problem. The action-primitive-based stage estimator and MMoE value decoder are well-motivated and empirically validated. The MoE-Decoder vs MoE-FFN analysis is thorough and counterintuitive (MoE belongs in output head, not FFN, for reward modeling). However, policy improvement experiments are limited to 2 tasks (folding shorts, cleaning whiteboard), and folding from crumpled remains challenging (4/12). No explicit code release. Falls short of featured threshold due to narrower experimental scope and moderate novelty.
risks_or_uncertainties: Policy improvement validated on only 2 tasks — generalizability of SPIRAL to diverse manipulation tasks unclear
Folding shorts from crumpled still at 4/12 after 3 SPIRAL rounds — hard tasks remain hard
Reward model adaptation requires 2-3 hours of human annotation per 100 rollouts (one-time but still costly)
Action-primitive vocabulary (21 primitives) may not cover all manipulation behaviors
No code release mentioned; architecture details insufficient for exact reproduction

candidates.title: LadderMan: Learning Humanoid Perceptive Ladder Climbing
candidates.abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise for operating in human-centered environments, yet ladder climbing remains one of the most challenging tasks due to sparse footholds and handholds, complex whole-body coordination, and sensitivity to perception and control errors. We present \textbf{LadderMan}, a unified system that enables humanoid robots to robustly climb diverse ladders and perform manipulation under such constrained conditions. Our climbing policy is built on a scalable two-stage learning pi

embodied_relevance.evidence: Enables humanoid robots (Unitree G1) to robustly climb diverse ladders and perform on-ladder manipulation (painting adjustment, light bulb replacement, box handover). Directly advances whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation capability.

primary_source.evidence: Original research presenting LadderMan with four novel components: hybrid motion tracking from single reference, DAgger+RL distillation, VFM-based depth perception for sim-to-real, and dual-agent on-ladder manipulation. Full experimental validation in simulation and on real hardware.

incremental_contribution.evidence: First visuomotor policy for humanoid ladder climbing that generalizes across ladder geometries (inclination 65-80 degrees, rung spacing 25-35cm). Hybrid motion tracking enables learning multiple experts from single reference motion. VFM (Fast FoundationStereo) replaces extensive depth randomization. Dual-agent manipulation decouples balance from upper-body tasks.

claim_support.evidence: >95% sim success across wide range of ladder configurations vs 49% peak for blind baseline. Real-world results: 9/10 Ladder A, 6/10 Ladder B, 7/10 Ladder C. Ablation shows w/o RL drops to 0-2/10, w/o VFM to 0-3/10, w/o RFM to 0/10. Human-comparable climbing speed demonstrated.

fulltext_for_recommendation.evidence: Read Method (Section 3: hybrid motion tracking, unified climbing policy via DAgger+RL, VFM depth sim-to-real, dual-agent manipulation), Experiments (Section 4: sim evaluation, ablation studies, real-world results), and Conclusion (Section 5).

candidates.selection_reason: Impressive demonstration of humanoid ladder climbing with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. The hybrid motion tracking approach (learning multiple experts from a single reference motion) is elegant and practical. VFM-based depth perception is a clever alternative to extensive depth randomization. On-ladder manipulation via dual-agent learning is a bonus. Falls just short of featured (79 vs 80 threshold) due to limited baseline comparison for climbing (only blind motion tracking), real-world evaluation on only 3 ladders with 10 trials each, and vertical ladder climbing not yet achieved.
risks_or_uncertainties: Climbing limited to inclined ladders (up to 80 degrees); vertical ladders not demonstrated and require different strategies
On-ladder manipulation limited by lack of dexterous end-effectors (no fingers)
Real-world evaluation on only 3 specific ladders with 10 trials each — limited statistical power
VFM (Fast FoundationStereo) requires external RTX 4090 GPU — not fully onboard
Teleoperation-based manipulation policy requires VR headset and trackers for deployment
Collision geometry fidelity identified as critical but hard to generalize across robot models

candidates.title: Scalable Behavior Cloning with Open Data, Training, and Evaluation
candidates.abstract: We introduce ABC, a fully open-source stack for manipulation with behavior cloning. At its core is ABC-130K: the largest open-source teleoperation dataset to date, featuring 3,500 hours of data spanning over 130K episodes across 195 diverse tasks. Furthermore, we open-source our accessible hardware setup, training infrastructure, and simulation pipeline. We also release 400 hours of sim-teleop data and provide a co-training recipe that produces correlated simulation and real-world evaluation, of

embodied_relevance.evidence: Open, end-to-end stack for behavior cloning in robot manipulation. ABC-130K dataset (3,500 hours, 130K+ episodes, 195 tasks) enables training of dexterous bimanual policies. ABC-DiT and ABC-VLA models execute tasks like credit card extraction, pen insertion, box folding.

primary_source.evidence: Original research releasing ABC-130K (largest open teleoperation dataset), ABC-Models (DiT and VLA variants), ABC-Sim (simulation pipeline with sim-to-real correlation), and DAgger infrastructure. Systematic architecture study across vision encoders, conditioning schemes, and batch sizes.

incremental_contribution.evidence: Largest open-source bimanual dexterous manipulation dataset by significant margin (3,500h vs MolmoAct2 720h). Systematic architecture comparison: DiT vs VLA, cross-attention vs adaLN vs FAST conditioning. Novel DAgger infrastructure using only passive leader arms (no additional hardware). Sim-to-real correlation validated (Pearson r=0.87).

claim_support.evidence: Architecture ablations evaluated on 3 real-world tasks with 50 trials each. Offline metrics (training loss, validation action error) correlated with real-world performance. Sim-to-real strict success correlation r=0.87, progress correlation r=0.93. Single-task fine-tuning results for credit cards (ABC-VLA), LEGO sorting, pen insertion, bottle cap unscrewing.

fulltext_for_recommendation.evidence: Read Method (Section 3: ABC-DiT, ABC-VLA architectures, scaling study, offline metrics), Real-World Capabilities (Section 5: single-task fine-tuning, DAgger self-improvement), and Infrastructure (Section 7). Full appendices with dataloader, architecture, and conditioning details.

candidates.selection_reason: Essential infrastructure paper for the embodied AI community. Fully open-source release (data, models, code, sim, evaluation) sets a new standard. ABC-130K at 3,500 hours is nearly 5x larger than the next open bimanual dataset. Systematic architecture comparison provides practical guidance for practitioners. Sim-to-real correlation validation enables researchers without hardware to iterate. The DAgger infrastructure using only passive leader arms is a clever practical contribution. While the architectural insights are incremental, the open infrastructure impact justifies featured status.
risks_or_uncertainties: YAM robot platform ($2K arms) may not be widely adopted; dataset transferability to other embodiments unclear
Architectural findings (DiT more compute-efficient, VLA benefits more from large batch sizes) may be specific to this data distribution
Tasks are mostly tabletop bimanual; mobile manipulation and navigation not covered
3,500 hours still small compared to industrial-scale datasets (e.g., GR00T N1 used much larger proprietary data)
Pieter Abbeel is NOT listed as first author but may be a contributor — paper lists many authors from unnamed institutions

Egocentric human videos offer a scalable source of diverse manipulation behaviors, but directly using them for robot learning requires bridging two gaps: the visual gap between human and robot observations, and the action gap between human motion and robot-executable action. candidates.abstract: Going beyond predicting robot actions, World Action Models (WAMs) can also generate future visual observations. candidates.abstract: High-quality demonstration data are essential for humanoid robot skill learning, especially for whole-body behaviors that require coordinated perception, locomotion, and manipulation. candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a prominent framework for developing driving experts in autonomous vehicles. candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for generalizable robotic manipulation. candidates.abstract: Motion feasibility prediction plays a central role in robotics, particularly in task and motion planning and manipulation. candidates.abstract: Robotic manipulators operating in unstructured environments face significant challenges in safely executing goal-directed tasks due to dynamic and unforeseen obstacles, while traditional methods rely on prior knowledge or fixed perception pipelines, limiting adaptability. candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for locomotion frequently converges to locally optimal but undeployable behaviors, such as vibrating limbs or scooting on the torso, that maximize return without producing a usable gait. candidates.abstract: Mobile manipulators need world models that are current, queryable, semantically meaningful, and usable under edge-compute constraints. candidates.abstract: Object-Goal Navigation (ObjNav) requires embodied agents to autonomously locate specified targets using only egocentric visual observations. candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are emerging robotic control systems that integrate perception, language understanding, and action generation in a unified architecture. candidates.abstract: Human demonstrations for robot imitation learning often contain mistakes and corrective behaviors, such as imprecise grasps, object misalignment, unstable contact, and repeated attempts. candidates.abstract: Simulator-in-the-loop optimization offers a promising inference-time mechanism for robot manipulation. candidates.abstract:

candidates.abstract: Conventional visual navigation policies often struggle with myopic decision-making and mode collapse in complex environments. candidates.abstract: Robotics increasingly relies on GPUs for parallel simulation, large-scale learning, and neural-network inference. candidates.abstract: Human-hand demonstrations provide a direct and scalable source of physical interaction data for robot learning. candidates.abstract:

candidates.abstract: Imitation learning for robotic manipulation relies on large sets of human demonstration trajectories, which are often noisy and temporally irregular due to variable operator speed, intermittent pauses, and inconsistent action density. candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable robots to execute manipulation tasks from natural-language instructions grounded in visual observations. candidates.abstract: Continuum robots offer strong potential for manipulation tasks due to their high degrees of freedom, compliant structures, and operational safety. candidates.abstract: World action models (WAMs) have recently shown promise in jointly modeling future observations and executable robot actions. candidates.abstract: Wet-lab robots can improve the reproducibility, throughput, and safety of biomedical experiments, but scaling their learning requires customizable simulators for safe and reproducible task generation, open editable laboratory assets, and efficient pipelines that turn limited demonstrations into usable training data. candidates.abstract: Robotic table tennis is a representative benchmark for high-speed, closed-loop robotic control in dynamic environments, where accurate and fast prediction of ball states is critical for reliable planning and control. candidates.abstract: Action chunking has become a standard design in modern robot policies, from diffusion/flow policies to vision-language-action models, where the policy predicts a sequence of actions and executes a fixed number of them instead of acting one step at a time. candidates.abstract: Piezoresistive tactile sensors are attractive for robotic manipulation because they are thin, lightweight, low-cost, and scalable to dense large-area sensing. candidates.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires robots to continuously perceive and regulate evolving physical interactions under dynamic contact transitions or complex surface geometries. candidates.abstract: Assistive mobility and manipulation platforms have received increasing attention as a means of restoring independence to individuals with disabilities. candidates.abstract: Lifelong embodied navigation in dynamic environments requires robots to form persistent scene understanding from fragmentary observations, which remains difficult for existing methods that rely on explicit maps or scene graphs and struggle to generalize beyond structured settings. candidates.abstract: Learning-based visual navigation for legged robots typically relies on continuous goal updates from hierarchical state estimation to provide a persistent directional reference. candidates.title: IMPACT: Learning Internal-Model Predictive Control for Forceful Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Real-world robotic manipulation tasks often involve forceful interactions with the environment, such as using tools of varying weights, transporting objects with different masses, and performing contact-rich tasks like table wiping. candidates.abstract: Robotic foundation models pre-trained on human demonstration videos have shown promise, but a significant embodiment gap remains when the resulting policies are deployed on real robots. candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong promise for robotic manipulation, but their reliability at test time remains limited by one-shot action prediction, where even small action errors can cause grasp failure, collision, or incorrect task progression. candidates.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a new powerful paradigm for embodied intelligence, learning action-relevant visual dynamics that significantly enhance generalization and robustness. We present OpenEAI-Platform, a fully open-source platform that integrates a low-cost 6+1 degree-of-freedom (dof) robotic arm (OpenEAI-Arm) and a reproducible VLA model (OpenEAI-VLA). OpenEAI-Arm provides open-source mechanical designs for low manufacturing cost and compliant control methods for higher accuracy. candidates.title: Autonomous Navigation System for Library Service Robot Based on Unitree Go2 Edu
candidates.abstract: Libraries require autonomous robots to move quietly through narrow aisles while remaining safe around readers, chairs, bags, and carts. This paper presents a ROS 2 navigation system for a Unitree Go2 Edu quadruped equipped with a 4D LiDAR, a front depth camera, and an IMU. candidates.title: EaDex: A Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation Framework from Low-Cost Demonstrations
candidates.abstract: Dexterous manipulation learning has long been hindered by the high costs of data and training, as pure reinforcement learning typically requires large-scale interactive exploration and imitation learning depends on high-quality demonstrations that are expensive to collect. candidates.title: AirDreamer: Generalist Drone Navigation with World Models
candidates.abstract: Navigating a drone in unseen and cluttered environments requires reliable generalization to unseen scene layouts and understanding of environmental structure relative to the robot's capabilities. Previous methods, which assume the same environment configuration, often rely heavily on human-designed perception pipelines and predefined rules to guide the robot toward the target. candidates.title: Intercepting the Future: Latent-Space Predictive World Model for Dynamic VLA Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generalize across static manipulation but fail when objects move during task execution. They map the current observation to an action and assume the scene is stationary between observation and execution, so at any non-trivial object speed the resulting latency exceeds the time available to grasp. candidates.title: FATE-VLA:Failue-aware test generation for vision-language-action models
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are increasingly used as generalist robot policies, yet their evaluation still relies largely on static benchmarks that randomly sample task scenes. In high-dimensional embodied spaces, failures are sparse and clustered, so static benchmarking can underestimate robustness risks. candidates.title: RoboSemanticBench: Diagnosing Semantic Grounding in Action Prediction for VLA Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are built on the premise that semantic understanding from pretrained language or vision-language backbones should guide robot action prediction. Yet robot fine-tuning is optimized as imitation over task-specific action distributions, and many evaluations can be solved through visual or instruction-action shortcuts. candidates.title: Dexterity-BEV: Aligning 3D World and Actions for Generalizable Robot Policies Learning
candidates.abstract: End-to-end manipulation policies, combined with web-scale pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs), show the promise for generalizable and dexterous robotic manipulation. However, they inherit two key limitations from 2D foundation models: 1) the reliance on 2D RGB inputs that ignores the intrinsically 3D nature of manipulation; and 2) the lack of spatial 3D alignment between input-output spaces as well as across diverse robot embodiments, camera setups, and trajectory datasets. candidates.title: Motion Planning in Dynamic Environments: A Survey from Classical to Modern Methods
candidates.abstract: Motion planning in dynamic environments requires robots to continuously adapt their paths in response to environmental changes for safe and uninterrupted navigation. While many surveys have reviewed planning in static settings, systematic reviews focused on dynamic environments remain limited. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of 138 works, primarily published between 2015 and 2025, spanning both classical and learning-based approaches. candidates.title: WALL-WM: Carving World Action Modeling at the Event Joints
candidates.abstract: WALL-WM is a World Action Model that shifts video-action learning from chunk-centric optimization to event-grounded Vision-Language-Action pretraining, using semantically coherent action events as the atomic unit of learning. candidates.title: Set-Supervised Diffusion Policy: Learning Action-Chunking Diffusion through Corrections
candidates.abstract: Diffusion policies have recently emerged as a powerful framework for robotic manipulation. However, like other behavior cloning methods, they remain vulnerable to distributional shift, often requiring human-in-the-loop interventions to correct failures during deployment. candidates.title: IMAGIN-4D: Image-Guided Controllable Interaction Generation
candidates.abstract: Generating human-object interactions (HOI) is central to character animation, robotics, AR/VR, and embodied AI. Recent HOI generation methods synthesize motion from text, object geometry, and sparse waypoints, controlling action semantics and object trajectories. candidates.title: How Should World Models Be Evaluated for Embodied Decision-Making? A Decision-Making-Centric Position
candidates.abstract: World models have become a central abstraction in modern AI. The term now refers to several different objects: action-conditioned environment models, latent imagination models, future-video predictors, interactive neural simulators, latent predictive representations, and synthetic-data engines. candidates.title: LeCropFollow: Latent Space Planning for Navigation in Unstructured Crop Fields
candidates.abstract: Unstructured navigational features, such as irregular planting or discontinuities, remain the primary failure mode for under-canopy agricultural robots. Existing geometric approaches often fail in these scenarios because they compress high-dimensional visual data into deterministic spatial references, effectively discarding the uncertainty and semantic context required to navigate ambiguous terrain. candidates.title: Learning Locomotion on Discrete Terrain via Minimal Proximity Sensing
candidates.abstract: Learning-based control has revolutionized dynamic locomotion, yet navigating unstructured terrain remains limited by a robot's incomplete awareness of imminent ground contact. While global perception systems such as LiDARs and depth cameras provide environmental context, they are frequently plagued by latencies, occlusions, and the high computational cost of dense geometric reconstruction. candidates.title: FastDSAC: Enhancing Policy Plasticity via Constrained Exploration for Scalable Humanoid Locomotion
candidates.abstract: Scalable reinforcement learning has popularized high-throughput sampling architectures, which significantly compresses the training time for off-policy methods in robotic locomotion. However, the rapid increase of data volume and update frequency undermines the stability of value-based methods and diminishes the plasticity of policy networks. candidates.title: Revisiting Parameter Redundancy in Vision-Language-Action Models: Insights from VLM-to-VLA Adaptation
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made significant strides in embodied intelligence by integrating the powerful representations of pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs). However, the massive parameter scale of VLAs imposes a heavy computational burden, and these models exhibit extreme sensitivity to parameter pruning. candidates.title: Plan Right, Then Plan Tight: Symbolic RL for Efficient Embodied Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Embodied task planning asks an agent to turn a natural-language instruction into an executable sequence of actions in a physical scene, and is a building block for household, assistive, and service robots. Recent prompting-based and reinforcement-learning planners generate fluent action text but lack a cheap deterministic check that the produced plan is valid in the target world, while high-fidelity simulation is too slow to serve as an inner-loop training signal. candidates.title: Warp RL: Reshaping Base Policy Distributions for Dynamics Adaptation
candidates.abstract: Residual reinforcement learning adapts a pretrained robot policy by learning an additive correction to its actions. While effective when adaptation amounts to shifting the base policy's action distribution, additive corrections cannot change the distribution's shape, scale, or state-dependent geometry -- limitations we formalize as wrong variance, miscalibrated confidence, and non-uniform correction. candidates.title: MOAR Planner: Multi-Objective and Adaptive Risk-Aware Path Planning for Infrastructure Inspection with a UAV
candidates.abstract: The problem of autonomous navigation for UAV inspection remains challenging as it requires effectively navigating in close proximity to obstacles, while accounting for dynamic risk factors such as weather conditions, communication reliability, and battery autonomy. This paper introduces the MOAR path planner which addresses the complexities of evolving risks during missions. candidates.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: Experimental Insights from a Real-World UR5 Platform
candidates.abstract: This project investigates whether recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can be transferred from controlled research benchmarks to a real-world robotic platform, specifically a UR5e manipulator, in a reproducible and operationally meaningful manner. candidates.title: Flying to Image-Specified Objects: 3D Quadrotor Navigation via Cross-Graph Memory and Viewpoint Planning
candidates.abstract: Instance-Specific Image-Goal Navigation (InstanceImageNav) requires a robot to navigate toward the exact object instance depicted in a query image. Extending this task to quadrotors is challenging due to continuous 3D control, limited field of view (FOV), and safety constraints, which make successful navigation highly dependent on selecting informative viewpoints. candidates.title: Analyzing Uncertainty in the Spatial Representation of the Kinematic Bicycle Model
candidates.abstract: Locating a vehicle and determining its orientation in an uncertain environment is a critical challenge in autonomous vehicle navigation and path planning. To address these challenges, a vehicle estimates its pose while depending on sensor data that offer noisy measurements. candidates.title: CORE: Common Outcome Regularities from Action-Free Visual Demonstrations for Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Robot imitation learning often relies on costly robot demonstrations, while abundant action-free visual demonstrations, such as human videos, are difficult to use because they lack robot-executable actions and suffer from embodiment gaps. We propose CORE, a policy learning framework that extracts Common Outcome Regularities from visual demonstrations. candidates.title: Position: Vision-Language-Action Models Cannot Be Verified to Perform Physical Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) systems, built on pretrained vision-language models (VLMs), have shown rapidly improving performance on robot manipulation benchmarks. These gains are commonly interpreted as evidence that semantic representations learned from internet-scale data transfer to physical execution generalization. candidates.title: LAMP: Long-Horizon Adaptive Manipulation Planning for Multi-Robot Collaboration in Cluttered Space
candidates.abstract: Multi-robot manipulation requires jointly reasoning about contact formations, robot motions under coupled dynamics, and collision avoidance. Systematically searching over this large space is difficult and becomes increasingly intractable as the number of robots grows, the task horizon lengthens, or the scene becomes more densely cluttered. candidates.title: TAP-VLA: Tactile Annotation Prompting for Vision Language Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models demonstrate impressive reasoning over visual, semantic, and spatial task variations by leveraging large-scale vision and language pre-training. They remain, however, largely blind to contact forces, which seldom manifest clearly in visual feedback but are central to contact-rich manipulation. candidates.title: A Unified Framework for Multi-Contact Path Planning in the Rolling Robot Systems
candidates.abstract: Rolling motion planning is challenging because rolling contact imposes nonholonomic constraints and the configuration evolves on a curved manifold. The problem becomes substantially harder in multi-contact settings, where multiple bodies roll without slip and the contact states are coupled. This paper presents a new framework for multi-contact path planning in spherical rolling robotics under no-slip constraints. candidates.title: He3-Seeker: Robotic Information Planning for Lunar Helium-3 Distribution Mapping
candidates.abstract: Lunar helium-3 is a highly valuable strategic resource, pivotal to the advancement of both deep-space exploration and space mining. Existing lunar helium-3 exploration methodologies rely primarily on indirect measurements via remote sensing, which are often characterized by limited precision, low reliability, and insufficient spatial resolution. candidates.title: CacheMPC: Certified Cached Model Predictive Control for Quadruped Locomotion
candidates.abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) is the standard predictive layer in hierarchical quadruped controllers, but the per-cycle QP solve limits the update rate achievable on embedded processors. Because legged gaits revisit a bounded region of state space, MPC solutions admit caching and reuse. candidates.title: Unleashing Infinite Motion: Scaling Expressive Quadrupedal Motion via Generative Video Priors
candidates.abstract: Quadruped robots have achieved remarkable locomotion, yet their behavioral repertoire remains confined to a few gaits--far from the expressive, companion-like presence long envisioned for them. candidates.title: Building a Scalable, Reproducible, Evaluatable, and Closed-Loop Simulation Environment Foundation for Embodied Intelligence
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a cloud-native simulation infrastructure framework for embodied intelligence that supports large-scale training, standardized evaluation, and simulation-based data collection. The framework unifies simulation environment generation, task execution, trajectory collection, model evaluation, data management, and cloud services into a scalable and reproducible platform. candidates.title: Drop-Then-Recovery: How Redundant Are Vision-Language-Action Models?
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable instruction-driven robotic manipulation, but they inherit oversized language backbones from pretrained VLMs whose capacity far exceeds what is needed for short robotic instructions. This raises a basic question: how much of a VLA model is actually necessary for closed-loop control? candidates.title: Direct Action-Head Injection of A Grounded 3D Point Unlocks Spatial and Task Generalization
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage large-scale vision-language pretraining for flexible robot manipulation, yet at test time they remain brittle along two axes: spatial generalization, when object positions differ from those seen during training, and task generalization, when a familiar scene is paired with a different language instruction than the one seen in training. candidates.title: Learning to Throw: Agile and Accurate Cable-Suspended Payload Delivery with a Quadrotor
candidates.abstract: Quadrotors offer the agility needed to rapidly transport suspended payloads during time-critical applications, including search-and-rescue and medical delivery. While suspended-payload transport and traversal for these missions are well studied, the highly dynamic targeted release of the payload remains comparatively underexplored. candidates.title: Learning 3D Affordances for Blade Insertion in Cluttered Stowing
candidates.abstract: Many manipulation tasks require reasoning about free-space affordances: discovering volumes where an extended rigid tool can safely navigate, complementary to surface contact affordances for grasping. Robotic stowing is a canonical instance, where a blade must sweep items aside inside cluttered fabric bins to create insertion space. candidates.title: Bridging Performance and Generalization in Reinforcement Learning for Agile Flight
candidates.abstract: Autonomous drone racing is a fundamentally challenging regime for autonomous aerial robots, requiring time-optimal control while operating under persistent actuation saturation. candidates.title: LA4VLA: Learning to Act without Seeing via Language-Action Pretraining
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are commonly pretrained on robot demonstrations by jointly mapping visual observations and language instructions to actions. However, dense visual-action supervision can dominate the comparatively sparse language-action signal. candidates.title: E-TTS: A New Embodied Test-Time Scaling Framework for Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Recently, a few works have made early attempts to study test-time scaling for embodied tasks. However, two major challenges remain unsolved: (1) reasoning can effectively improve the performance of the policy, but its scaling mechanism has seldom been studied; (2) historical information is essential, as embodied tasks are inherently long-horizon and sequential, making sole reliance on current observations for action scaling inadequate due to the lack of historical context utilization. candidates.title: Learning to Fold: prizewinning solution at LeHome Challenge 2026 (1st place online, 2nd offline)
candidates.abstract: I describe my solution to the LeHome Challenge 2026, an ICRA 2026 competition on bimanual garment folding. The system placed 1st of 62 teams in the online (simulation) round and 2nd in the real-world final. It improves a vision-language-action (VLA) policy with a reinforcement-learning loop. candidates.title: PhysReflect-VLA: Physical Feasibility and Self-Reflective Regulation for Reliable Vision-Language-Action Policies
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation is highly sensitive to physically infeasible transitions, contact-induced disturbances, and the lack of effective self-correction during execution. Although Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models provide strong task grounding through multimodal learning, they typically generate actions in a feed-forward manner without explicitly checking physical feasibility or diagnosing execution errors online. candidates.title: PAMAE: Phase-Aware-MoE Action Experts Towards Reliable Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Policies
candidates.abstract: Reliable action generation for multi-stage robotic manipulation remains challenging for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. While existing flow-matching VLA policies offer strong multimodal grounding and generalization, they typically employ a single shared action expert, limiting their ability to capture phase-specific control patterns across distinct execution stages. candidates.title: ForesightSafety-VLA: A Unified Diagnostic Safety Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: In embodied intelligence, safety is a prerequisite for reliable robot deployment in the physical world. Current vision-language-action (VLA) models continue to advance toward general-purpose task capability, yet their embodied safety limits remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we introduce ForesightSafety-VLA, a diagnostic benchmark that makes safety the primary evaluation target for VLA systems. candidates.title: RelAfford6D: Relational 6D Affordance Graphs for Constraint-Driven Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Bridging abstract semantics and precise physical control remains a fundamental challenge in open-world robotic manipulation. While recent data-driven policies show promise, their reliance on isolated contact points or latent affordance embeddings lacks the rigorous kinematic constraints necessary for complex articulated objects.To overcome the limitation, we introduce RelAfford6D, a novel training-free framework centered on a Relational 6D Affordance Graph. candidates.title: Humanoid-DART: Humanoid Loco-Manipulation using Diffusion-guided Augmentation through Relabeling and Tracking
candidates.abstract: Imitating human demonstrations has emerged as a dominant paradigm for learning humanoid loco-manipulation policies. However, scaling these approaches remains challenging due to the high cost of collecting diverse demonstrations and the need for continual human intervention to correct policy failures. candidates.title: PressMimic: Pressure-Guided Motion Capture and Control for Humanoid Robot Imitation
candidates.abstract: Humanoid motion imitation requires not only accurate perception of human kinematics but also faithful reproduction of physical interactions with the environment. candidates.title: Bridging Handheld and Teleoperated Supervision for Contact-Rich Manipulation via State-Gated Experts
candidates.abstract: Handheld data collection systems, such as the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI), enable scalable data collection across diverse environments but only capture observed actions rather than the desired actions executed by a robot controller. candidates.title: A System for Fast, Resilient, and Adaptable Loco-Manipulation Behaviors on Humanoid Robots
candidates.abstract:
Humanoid robots could take on physically demanding, hazardous, and repetitive work in spaces built for humans. However, a useful robot for these spaces must coordinate locomotion, whole body motion, perception, contact, and operator supervision. This thesis presents a robot-local, runtime-editable behavior authoring and runtime system.

candidates.abstract: Long-horizon, contact-rich complex manipulation tasks, such as seating a GPU into a PCIe slot, demand both millimeter high precision and out-of-the-box generalization to new tasks. candidates.title: Racing a Wheeled Quadruped: Active Load Transfer Mitigation via Model Predictive Control
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical control framework using model predictive control (MPC) and reinforcement learning (RL) for active roll control to manage lateral load transfer during autonomous racing of a wheeled quadruped. candidates.title: NavIsaacLab: Generating Realistic Crowd via Parallel Robot Learning for Benchmarking Human-aware Navigation
candidates.abstract: Robot autonomous navigation that accounts for surrounding human activities is crucial for ensuring both safety and natural human-robot interaction in real-world environments shared by humans and robots. candidates.title: Learning Action Priors for Cross-embodiment Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models build on a Vision-Language Model (VLM) backbone by attaching an action module and optimizing the full policy jointly. candidates.title: OmniContact: Chaining Meta-Skills via Contact Flow for Generalizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Learning long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation poses a dual challenge: it requires not only the robust execution of meta-skills but also their seamless, closed-loop chaining equipped with autonomous recovery. candidates.title: Action ControlNet: A Lightweight Delay-Aware Adapter for Smooth Asynchronous Control in Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for general-purpose robot manipulation, but their inference latency remains a major obstacle to stable high-frequency control. candidates.title: Mixture-of-Experts RL for Fault-Tolerant Legged Locomotion
candidates.abstract: Legged robots deployed in planetary exploration and other remote environments must maintain reliable locomotion despite actuator failures and challenging terrain conditions. Although reinforcement learning has achieved strong results in legged locomotion, monolithic policies can struggle to efficiently represent the diverse control strategies required to compensate for different fault conditions. candidates.title: ROAD-VLA: Robust Online Adaptation via Self-Distillation for Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Effective online adaptation of vision-language-action (VLA) models remains challenging, as sparse rewards provide weak supervision for high-dimensional autoregressive action policies. candidates.title: Learning Asynchronous Upper-body Task-space Trajectory Tracking Policy for Humanoid Robots
candidates.abstract: High-level humanoid planners often output sparse task-space, low-rate trajectories, whereas whole-body controllers run at high frequency. This creates temporal asynchrony between the planning and execution, and structural incompleteness for full-body control. candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for robotic manipulation often requires manually designing a dense reward function, which is difficult to tune and often fragile, or learning a reward from human demonstrations or preferences, which can be expensive. candidates.abstract: Robot navigation in safety-critical scenarios faces significant challenges from unforeseen semantic events, where collisions arise primarily from the unpredictable behaviors of dynamic agents rather than unseen objects. candidates.abstract: Reward design remains a major bottleneck in reinforcement learning for robot locomotion, where successful policies often depend on carefully tuned, task-specific reward functions. candidates.abstract: Universal quadrupedal locomotion remains limited by the difficulty of integrating perception across diverse robot morphologies. State-of-the-art controllers rely on single-robot training or blind policies that omit real-time perception, leading to poor cross-embodiment generalization. candidates.title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models can learn manipulation skills from demonstrations, but their capabilities are bounded by the skills in the training data. candidates.abstract: The development of trajectory planning strategies for autonomous ground vehicles (AGVs) represents a prevailing research interest within the domain of intelligent transportation systems. candidates.title: ArtiTwinSplat: Interactable Digital Twin Reconstruction via Gaussian Splatting from RGB-D videos
candidates.abstract: Deploying robots in unstructured real-world environments needs accurate, interactive models of the objects. Constructing these models at scale remains a critical bottleneck for robotic system integration. We present ArtiTwinSplat, a framework that automatically constructs articulated, photo-realistic digital twins of objects directly from RGB-D videos, requiring no CAD models, simulation assets, or manual annotations. candidates.abstract: Autonomous microrobots navigating biological vasculature could enable targeted drug delivery and thrombolysis, yet training control policies for realistic environments remains an open challenge. candidates.title: SlipSense: Multimodal Sensing for Online Slip Detection in Legged Robots
candidates.abstract: Legged robots rely on accurate ground interaction awareness to traverse variable terrains, such as slippery surfaces. Existing slip detection methods often rely on kinematics and proprioception, which lack the sensitivity to detect early-stage slips that occur prior to catastrophic instability. candidates.title: DynaWM: Dynamics-Aware Distillation with World Model and Momentum Targets for Smooth Locomotion over Continuous Stairs
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in control have enabled bipedal-wheeled robots to traverse slopes and single-step obstacles, yet long staircase traversal remains challenging as current teacher-student frameworks suffer from weakened dynamics-aware representations and incomplete terrain geometry encoding. candidates.title: MinInter: Minimizing Trajectory Interpolation During Data Augmentation for Imitation Learning
candidates.abstract: Imitation learning enables robots to acquire complex manipulation skills from demonstrations, but its effectiveness is limited by the cost of collecting high-quality data. Trajectory-level data augmentation methods alleviate this challenge by recombining expert demonstrations under varied initial states. However, such methods typically insert interpolations or other non-expert transition segments between disjoint parts, and such non-expert segments could reduce the quality of the generated data.

candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are commonly fine-tuned through passive imitation learning, where additional demonstrations are collected for tasks where the policy performs poorly. candidates.title: KEMO: Event-Driven Keyframe Memory for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation with VLA Policies
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation remains challenging because similar observations may occur at different execution stages, while the appropriate action depends on previously completed operations. Memory can address this ambiguity by enabling policies to infer task progress from execution history. candidates.title: Flowing With Purpose: Latent Action Guided Flow Matching Policies For Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Flow matching has recently become a new standard for behavior cloning in robotic manipulation. However, state-of-the-art flow matching policies suffer from a systematic structural mismatch: they rely on a globally fixed isotropic source distribution despite the strongly fragmented and heteroscedastic structure of robotic action spaces. This agnostic initialization forces the model to learn highly entangled vector fields, bottlenecking training efficiency and limiting overall policy performance.

candidates.title: TSD: A Physics-Inspired Trajectory Saliency Detector for Efficient Imitation Learning
candidates.abstract: For imitation learning in robotic manipulation, high data collection costs result in the scarcity of high quality data. In this paper, we leverage the inherent heterogeneity of trajectories to address this challenge. candidates.title: LP-NavOA: Integrated Local Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance for Humanoid Robots under Limited Perception
candidates.abstract: Humanoid local navigation in cluttered environments must jointly resolve obstacle avoidance, sparse-goal recovery, and stable whole-body locomotion under short-range and partially observable sensing. Explicit planner-control decompositions introduce latency and can mismatch agile humanoid command-tracking limits, while purely reactive controllers may lose the goal after obstacle occlusion. We present LP-NavOA, a limited-perception navigation and obstacle-avoidance framework for humanoid robots.

candidates.title: Foresight: Failure Detection for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation with Action-Conditioned World Model Latents
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon tasks are common in real-world robotic deployments, yet failure detection for such tasks remains underexplored. candidates.abstract: Neural world models coupled with model predictive control (MPC) replan at every environment step to bound accumulated prediction error, but this incurs substantial computational overhead. candidates.abstract: We present Cloak, a training recipe that endows a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model with zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer by cloaking the end-effector from its own wrist camera. The end-effector occupies a large and consistent region of the wrist view and masking it allows for embodiment-agnostic visual reasoning. candidates.title: Verifiable Foundation Models for Robot Safety
candidates.abstract: Deploying foundation models for robot control raises a central challenge: the expressive power that enables rich, multimodal perception also makes these models opaque and difficult to analyze formally, rendering them intractable for existing verification tools. candidates.abstract: Learning visuomotor policies for long-horizon manipulation remains a fundamental challenge. Recent skill-based imitation learning methods based on discrete quantization have shown promising results by representing complex behaviors as temporally extended skills. candidates.abstract: Robotic ultrasound scanning in real clinical environments requires both high-level clinical workflow reasoning and low-level closed-loop execution. Physicians natural-language instructions often contain implicit anatomical targets, procedural logic, image-quality requirements, and safety constraints, while execution is affected by patient motion, contact variations, and target drift. candidates.title: DeformX: A Versatile Co-Simulation Framework for Deformable Linear Objects
candidates.abstract: Deformable linear objects (DLOs) such as wires, cables, and ropes are common in robotic manipulation tasks, yet simulating them with both visual realism and physical accuracy remains challenging. candidates.abstract: Multi-task robot manipulation policies are challenging to learn from demonstration because traditionally a single network must select among qualitatively different action modes from a multimodal demonstration distribution, conditioned on language and visual context. candidates.title: Temporal logics and formal synthesis for robot planning and control
candidates.abstract: As robots move from controlled environments into real-world settings, it becomes increasingly crucial to ensure that they perform as expected. A key step toward that goal is a rigorous specification of the desired robot behavior, capturing intricate temporal, spatial, and logical requirements. candidates.abstract: A central question in robot learning is how to acquire skills from the kinds of data that humans learn from: passive observation, embodied practice, and the experience of failure. candidates.abstract: Human hand grasp adaptation depends mainly on the synergy between physical structure and biological feedback. candidates.abstract: TransEsophageal Echocardiography (TEE) is essential for diagnosing and guiding Structural Heart Disease (SHD) interventions. However, manual TEE manipulation demands significant operator expertise, is physically demanding, and exposes clinicians to radiation when performed alongside fluoroscopy. candidates.abstract: Dual-arm manipulation can improve throughput via parallel execution, but collecting bimanual demonstrations for training is costly and difficult. candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong performance in robotic manipulation, but reliable uncertainty quantification remains challenging, particularly under distribution shift. candidates.abstract: Quadruped robots are increasingly expected to navigate through narrow passages, cluttered indoor scenes, and large-scale 3D unstructured environments. candidates.abstract: Soft lattice structures are increasingly used in robotics to tailor compliance and guide deformation; however, actuation is typically introduced at the device or module level, with actuators inserted into otherwise passive architectures. candidates.abstract: Foundation models in language and multimodality achieve strong generalization by aligning heterogeneous data under a unified formulation and training at scale. However, existing AR brain-robot interface (BRI) systems are often constrained to task-specific structures, limiting their utility in real-world environments. candidates.title: FlowMPC: Improving Flow Matching policies with World Models
candidates.abstract: Flow Matching (FM) is a powerful approach for behavior cloning in multimodal action spaces [Jiang et al., 2025], but because it is not trained to directly maximize expected return, there is still room to improve how FM policies act at test time. This work investigates whether a learned world model can improve FM policies by enabling Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) planning over candidate action sequences proposed by the policy. candidates.title: ATHENA: Accelerated Multi-Task Heterogeneous Influence Functions for Robot Data Curation
candidates.abstract: In robot imitation learning, influence functions provide a principled approach to quantify each demonstration's effect on robot task outcomes, yet scaling them to billion-parameter Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models is limited by computational and multitask bottlenecks. To this end, we propose ATHENA, an influence function framework tailored for multitask VLA data curation at a billion-parameter scale. candidates.title: Energy-Efficient Arm Reaching for a Humanoid Robot via Deep Reinforcement Learning with Identified Power Models
candidates.abstract: Humanoid robots performing in-field manipulation tasks, such as robotic apple harvesting, face severe energy constraints that directly limit the number of reaching motions that can be executed per battery charge. candidates.title: Beyond English: Uncovering the Multilingual Gap in Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models have recently demonstrated promising capabilities in learning generalist robot policies from large-scale multimodal data. However, most existing VLA systems are trained and evaluated primarily with English instructions, leaving their ability to understand and execute instructions in other languages largely unexplored. candidates.title: PO-PDDL: Learning Symbolic POMDPs from Visual Demonstrations for Robot Planning Under Uncertainty
candidates.abstract: Real-world robot task planning must operate under both stochastic action execution and partial observability, yet constructing Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) models for real robotics domains remains difficult and labor-intensive. We introduce PO-PDDL, a symbolic formulation of POMDPs that preserves the relational structure and LLM-friendly syntax of the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), while explicitly modeling partial observability, stochasticity, and beliefs. candidates.title: Retrieve, Don't Retrain: Extending Vision Language Action Models to New Tasks at Test Time
candidates.abstract: Extending a vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a new task typically requires task-specific teleoperated demonstrations and per-task fine-tuning, making adaptation costly in both data collection and compute. In this paper, we show that this target-side per-task adaptation cost can be replaced by retrieval. candidates.abstract: We present SLS^2, a framework for safe feedback motion planning from pixels using robust model predictive control (MPC) in learned latent world models. Our approach trains an action-conditioned joint-embedding world model with compact Markovian latent states, enabling efficient gradient-based trajectory optimization through learned latent dynamics. candidates.title: Perfect Demo Makes Poor Teacher: Learning Robust Alignment from Critical Motion Segments
candidates.abstract: Expert demonstrations are widely assumed to be the gold standard for robot imitation learning. Yet for fine-grained manipulation such as insertion, stacking, and alignment, we uncover a counterintuitive failure mode: fluent demonstrations can be poor teachers. candidates.title: Robots as Tokens: Unified Diffusion Transformer for Coordinated Multi-Robot Trajectory Generation
candidates.abstract: The success of generative models in language and visual generation has inspired extensive applications to generative robot planning. However, most existing works either focus on single-robot planning, or generate multi-robot trajectories in a sequential manner with iterative post-processing to resolve inter-robot conflicts. candidates.title: Transferring Contact, Not Just Motion: Compliant Grasping Across Dexterous Hands
candidates.abstract: Dexterous grasping depends on contact regulation, not motion alone. Stable manipulation requires fingers to maintain appropriate object loading as contacts slip, deform, or become visually occluded. Existing cross-embodiment dexterous policies unify motion through retargeted hand poses or latent actions, but force feedback remains tied to each hand's sensing and actuation, limiting transfer. candidates.title: Acting While Understanding: Asynchronous Semantic-Action Decoupling for Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have demonstrated strong task understanding and generalization in robotic manipulation, yet the high computational cost of full-model inference limits their deployment in low-latency, high-frequency closed-loop control. candidates.title: Rethinking Implicit Spatial Representation in Visuomotor Policy Learning
candidates.abstract: Generative model-based imitation learning has become a widely adopted paradigm for robotic manipulation, where policy performance depends critically on the conditioned visual representations. Although spatial softmax-based representations have been adopted in prior visuomotor policies, their effectiveness and underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. candidates.title: Task-Aware Environment Augmentation for Reliable Navigation via Shielded Conditional Diffusion
candidates.abstract: Reliable trajectory planning under partial observability depends not only on computing a feasible geometric path, but also on whether the robot receives informative observations while executing that trajectory. candidates.title: Think Less, Act Early: Reinforced Latent Reasoning with Early Exit in Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models predominantly rely on explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning to bridge perception and action. While effective, this paradigm suffers from high computational costs and error propagation in multi-step tasks. candidates.title: Inference-time Policy Steering via Vision and Touch
candidates.abstract: Inference-time steering adapts pre-trained generative robot policies during deployment by verifying candidate actions before execution. While prior methods typically perform this verification only with visual observations, vision alone is often insufficient for contact-rich manipulation, where success depends on both global task progress and subtle local interactions such as contact force. candidates.title: VANDERER: Map-Free Exploration using Future-Aware and Visual-Curiosity-Guided Diffusion Policy
candidates.abstract: Mobile agents require efficient exploration strategies to map unseen environments and autonomously plan tasks. Traditional methods rely on generating occupancy maps and optimizing the sequence in which unexplored regions are visited. However, in sensor-constrained settings, such as those limited to monocular cameras, generating accurate occupancy maps is challenging. candidates.title: Sensitivity Shaping for Latent Modeling
candidates.abstract: Generative dynamics models enable planning in challenging robotic systems, but safe deployment requires reliably detecting policy-induced out-of-distribution (OOD) transitions. Existing methods typically treat the learned dynamics as fixed and attach post hoc support surrogates. candidates.title: TRACE: Trajectory-Routed Causal Memory for Delayed-Evidence Visuomotor Imitation
candidates.abstract: Robots under autonomous operation may require decisions based on evidence that is no longer visible. We study delayed-evidence tasks, where an early cue disappears before a later decision point, so visually similar observations can require different actions. candidates.title: FloVerse: Floor Plan-Guided Multi-Modal Navigation
candidates.abstract: Floor plans encapsulate compact spatial priors, enabling agents to navigate unseen scenes more efficiently. While prior work has explored floor plan-guided navigation, it has focused mainly on PointNav and a limited set of environments. To bridge this gap, we introduce FloVerse, a new task for floor plan-guided embodied navigation that unifies PointNav, ObjectNav, and ImageNav. candidates.title: ReactVLA: Fast and Lightweight Reactive Robot Manipulation via Improved Mean Flow Action Generation
candidates.abstract: Diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies have demonstrated strong capability in modeling expressive and multimodal action distributions. However, their reliance on iterative sampling introduces substantial inference latency, which limits their applicability to reactive closed-loop robot manipulation. candidates.title: Short-Horizon Position Accuracy of Single-Track Models: Implications for Motion Planning of Autonomous Vehicles
candidates.abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient vehicle models are essential for motion planning of autonomous vehicles, where positional accuracy directly affects trajectory feasibility and safety. However, the positional accuracy has not been systematically evaluated against real measurements. candidates.title: Self-Improving VLA Policies: Selected Diffusion Noise for Spurious-Robust Action Smoothing
candidates.abstract: Diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies enable strong generalization in robotic manipulation, but remain sensitive to spurious visual correlations and noisy action generation, leading to brittle behavior under perturbations. candidates.title: The N2D Haptic Glove: A Multi-Finger Glove for 2D Directional Force Feedback for Contact Rich Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Humans rely on directional fingertip forces to probe and regulate contact during manipulation, yet most wearable haptic gloves render only vibration or single-axis force, leaving force direction ambiguous. candidates.abstract: Autonomous UAV navigation is conventionally solved by pipelines that separate perception, mapping, and planning into distinct stages, which propagates errors, accumulates latency, and requires environment-specific retuning. candidates.title: QPILOTS: Efficient Test-Time Q-Steering for Flow Policies
candidates.abstract: Flow-matching and diffusion policies are expressive action generators, but optimizing them with temporal-difference reinforcement learning (RL) remains difficult. Effective policy extraction requires exploiting the critic's action gradient, yet directly backpropagating this signal through a multi-step denoising process can be numerically unstable. candidates.title: $μ_0$: A Scalable 3D Interaction-Trace World Model
candidates.abstract: World models that capture how actions induce physical change enable scalable robot learning without reliance on embodiment-specific action labels. Pixel-space video models provide broad visual priors but expend model capacity on dense appearance reconstruction, while direct action models require embodiment-specific labels that hinder scalability. candidates.abstract: Human communication is inherently multimodal, where language is often accompanied by non-verbal cues such as gestures to convey intentions. However, current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models treat robotic manipulation as a pure text-driven task, overlooking the important role of gestures in Human-Robot Interaction (HRI). candidates.title: Proprioceptive-visual correspondence enables self-other distinction in humanoid robots
candidates.abstract: Distinguishing self from others is a prerequisite for social intelligence, yet humanoid robots that increasingly share workspaces with humans still lack this ability. candidates.abstract: This paper proposes a novel regularization design to effectively smooth policy functions in reinforcement learning. While regularization that enhances ``global'' Lipschitz continuity was initially considered, it has been limited to ``local'' Lipschitz continuity due to a tradeoff between smoothness and expressiveness. candidates.title: FTP-1: A Generalist Foundation Tactile Policy Across Tactile Sensors for Contact-Rich Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Despite the success of vision-based generalist robotic policies, existing tactile-based policies remain tied to fixed embodiments and sensor setups. This is because tactile signals are highly heterogeneous across hardware, making cross-sensor generalization difficult. candidates.title: Towards Reliable Sequential Object Picking in Clutter: The Runner-up Solution to RGMC 2025
candidates.abstract: As a long-standing challenge in robotic manipulation, stable and efficient grasping in cluttered environments is of great importance in industrial settings. While recent studies have achieved relatively high success rates in grasping from clutter, there remain few mature solutions for more demanding tasks such as sequential object search and sorting. candidates.title: AIR-VLA+: Decoupling Movement and Manipulation via Cascaded Dual-Action Decoders with Asymmetric MoE for Aerial Robots
candidates.abstract: Aerial manipulation systems have long suffered from representation coupling in end-to-end control, as platform-level Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) movement and end-effector-level arm manipulation differ substantially in action scale, dynamics, and control objectives.
